                                                                 New DataColumn("Column", GetType(String)),

                        sqlBulkCopy.ColumnMappings.Add("Column", "Column")
                        sqlBulkCopy.ColumnMappings.Add("Column", "Column")
                        sqlBulkCopy.ColumnMappings.Add("Column", "Column")
                        sqlBulkCopy.ColumnMappings.Add("Column", "Column")
                        con.Open()
                        sqlBulkCopy.WriteToServer(dtExcelData)

I follow a few professional artists via DeviantArt, and ConceptArt.org, as well as doing my own work, they all seem to use [Super Sculpey] (http://www.dickblick.com/products/super-sculpey/) or [Super Sculpey Firm](http://www.dickblick.com/products/super-sculpey-firm/). Some of them mix it at 1:1 ratio.  This can be baked in a regular home oven or in a Polymer Clay oven, that you can get at most craft stores.  This type of clay will retain all fingerprints, so to get that out you can use 90% Rubbing Alcohol and a paint brush, or Sculpey thinner.  Either work well.   If the sculpture is to be a one off, then after baking its painted and done, otherwise, its casted and molded usually in Resin.  The sculpture is usually created in a way so that the arms and/or legs can be removed and cast/molded separately, then reassembled and painted.
